hints.TestSquares: var a [5]int; for i := range a { a[i] = i * i }; return a
hints.TestExtend: x = append(x, single); x = append(x, many...); return x
hints.TestDelete: Make a fresh slice so the caller's array is untouched: out := make([]int, 0, len(x)-(j-i)); out = append(out, x[:i]...); out = append(out, x[j:]...)
hints.TestCleanStates: out := make([]string, 0, len(names)); for _, n := range names { out = append(out, strings.TrimSpace(n)) }
hints.TestFlatten: Range over the records, then range over each record, appending every field.
hints.TestClone: out := make([]int, len(x)); copy(out, x) (or slices.Clone(x))

quiz.why: The low index is inclusive and the high index is exclusive.

quiz.q: Why must you write xs = append(xs, v)?
options: append may return a slice with a new underlying array
to avoid a compile error about unused results only
quiz.why: When capacity runs out, append allocates a new array and returns a header pointing to it.
